verdict.rationale: React ships official TypeScript typings via @types/react/@types/react-dom, which let TypeScript's built-in language service provide autocompletion and inline type errors for React code in editors, and React docs point to eslint-plugin-react-hooks for additional editor-time linting feedback. However, there's no dedicated React language server or IDE plugin described—support relies entirely on generic TS/JS tooling rather than a first-party language service integration. Missing for 10: evidence of a dedicated React language service or editor plugin, details on JSX-specific type-checking accuracy, and independent confirmation of autocompletion quality in real editors.
